acceptance: A decision table in context lists all 16 not_offered patches with: offer now, offer after a named prerequisite, reduce first, or decline, each with its reason and the dependency it waits on.
The owner approves the table (recorded in context with date) before any manifest change or upstream contact.
patches.json records the decisions: declined entries get upstream_state declined with the reason; deferred entries keep not_offered with a reason naming what they wait on.
One follow-up item per approved offer exists, each naming the patch, its upstream-ready reduction and the upstream rules it must meet.
Patches upstream has already replaced are listed for retirement through the documented refresh --retire path with equivalence evidence, not retired in this item.
context:
Purpose: lowers the risk that the next upstream release stops on a conflict, which would fail the core item sqlglot-e2e-first-release-certification (BenchBox-dev/BenchBox tracker; cross-tracker needs are not possible).

Decision gate (owner): approve the per-patch table before any manifest edit, and approve each upstream offer individually before any pull request or issue is opened on tobymao/sqlglot. Declining a patch is also an owner decision because it keeps maintenance cost in the fork.

Verification rubric: (1) the table covers exactly the not_offered set on main at review time (recount before approval); (2) downstream contract tests pass after the patches.json edits (upstream_state/upstream/upstream_reason rules in MAINTAINING.md, Manifest entries); (3) every follow-up offer item names upstream's requirements: Conventional Commits title ending with the agent model ([CLAUDE], [CODEX]), tests in tests/dialects that run on the real engine, minimal scope per AGENTS.md.

Guardrails: no pull request, issue or comment on tobymao/sqlglot from this item; never offer a patch that reads the fork's benchbox package or depends on one; never change carried patch content or order here; upstream links in patches.json must be tobymao/sqlglot pull request or issue URLs; an offered patch stays carried until upstream merges it and a refresh retires it.
description: 16 carried patches have upstream_state not_offered and nothing records when one became a candidate or prompts an offer. sqlite-date-day-arithmetic carried a DATE_SUB lowering marked 'a candidate'; upstream built its own (tobymao/sqlglot#8931) and the overlap stopped the v30.31.0 refresh (issue #88). Every carried patch upstream takes is one less that can conflict. This item is triage only: it produces an owner-approved decision per patch and the manifest changes that record it. Each approved upstream offer is a separate follow-up item, because the outcome depends on a repository the fork does not control. Dependency facts on main: offerable on their own (no carried dependency): postgres-extract-return-types, duckdb-order-by-all-keyword, databricks-primary-key-ordering, snowflake-regexp-replace-groups, empty-group-by-generator, bigquery-window-nulls-ordering. Need another patch offered first: sqlite-date-extraction (postgres-extract-return-types), sqlite-date-day-arithmetic (sqlite-temporal-lowering), spark-databricks-regexp-trunc (empty-group-by-generator, databricks-primary-key-ordering), sqlite-index-null-ordering (null-ordering-source-semantics). Depend on patches that read the fork's benchbox package (mark_date_columns) and cannot be offered until those are reduced: sqlite-date-integer-semantics, sqlite-date-literals, sqlite-set-operation-operands, sqlite-empty-group-by. Others: singlestore-json-integer-index (no SingleStore engine in CI), null-ordering-source-semantics (BenchBox semantics choice).
